info.title: Jina AI API
info.description:
One reference for three hosts, merged from each host's own OpenAPI spec:

- `api.jina.ai`: Search Foundation API, from https://api.jina.ai/openapi.json
- `r.jina.ai`: Reader API, from https://r.jina.ai/openapi.json
- `s.jina.ai`: Search API, from https://s.jina.ai/openapi.json

Every endpoint takes `Authorization: Bearer <your Jina API key>`. Get a key at https://jina.ai/?sui=apikey.

Best-in-class embeddings, rerankers and document models for multilingual and multimodal search.

## Capabilities

- **Text embeddings** — dense vectors for semantic search, similarity, clustering and classification, in 100+ languages.
- **Multimodal embeddings** — images, video, audio and PDFs embedded into the same space as text, so a query in one modality retrieves another.
- **Reranking** — score a query against a candidate set and reorder it; more accurate than embedding similarity, and the usual second stage after it.
- **Document OCR** — read a page image and return its content as text or markdown, with tables and layout preserved, over the OpenAI chat completions schema.
- **Batch embeddings** — the same embedding models over JSONL, asynchronously, for workloads too large to send inline.

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `GET /v1/models` requires a key:

```
Authorization: Bearer jina_YOUR_API_KEY
```

Get one at [jina.ai/api-dashboard/key-manager](https://jina.ai/api-dashboard/key-manager).

## Rate limits

Requests per minute and tokens per minute. Anything over a limit answers `429`.

| Endpoint | Free | Paid | Premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/embeddings` | 500 RPM · 1M TPM | 500 RPM · 10M TPM | 5,000 RPM · 100M TPM |
| `/v1/rerank` | 500 RPM · 1M TPM | 500 RPM · 10M TPM | 5,000 RPM · 100M TPM |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 100 RPM · 500K TPM | 100 RPM · 5M TPM | 1,000 RPM · 50M TPM |

## Errors

Failures carry a `detail`, a `code` from the table below and the `request_id` to quote in a support request. `/v1/chat/completions` is the exception: it answers in OpenAI's error envelope, with the same code inside it.

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `INPUT_INVALID_LABELS` | 400 | Invalid training labels |
| `INPUT_LABEL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 400 | Label limit exceeded: <current> labels provided, maximum <limit> allowed for your plan |
| `INPUT_MODEL_NOT_FOUND` | 400 | Model '<model>' not found |
| `INPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 400 | Input text exceeds the model's maximum of <max_tokens> tokens |
| `AUTH_INVALID_API_KEY` | 401 | Invalid API key |
| `AUTH_INVALID_FORMAT` | 401 | Invalid authorization format |
| `AUTH_MISSING_API_KEY` | 401 | Authentication required |
| `AUTHZ_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` | 403 | Insufficient account balance |
| `AUTHZ_RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 403 | Resource limit exceeded for your plan |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | <resource_type> '<resource_id>' not found or access denied |
| `CONFLICT_RESOURCE_BUSY` | 409 | <resource_type> '<resource_id>' is currently being modified |
| `RATE_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 429 | Concurrency limit exceeded: <current>/<limit> concurrent requests |
| `RATE_IP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 429 | IP rate limit exceeded |
| `RATE_REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 429 | Request rate limit exceeded: <current>/<limit> requests per minute |
| `RATE_TOKEN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 429 | Token rate limit exceeded: <current>/<limit> tokens per minute |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | An unexpected error occurred |
| `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Service temporarily unavailable |
| `SERVICE_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Service request timed out |

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description:
Specifies your preference for the response format.

Supported formats: 
- text/event-stream
- application/json or text/json
- text/plain

parameters.name: X-Cache-Tolerance
parameters.description: Sets internal cache tolerance in seconds if this header is specified with a integer.

parameters.name: X-No-Cache
parameters.description:
Ignores internal cache if this header is specified with a value.

Equivalent to X-Cache-Tolerance: 0

parameters.name: X-Respond-With
parameters.description:
Specifies the (non-default) form of the crawled data you prefer.

Supported formats: 
- markdown
- html
- text
- pageshot
- screenshot
- content
- frontmatter
- any combination of the above
- vlm
- jina-ocr-v1
- jina-ocr
- readerlm-v2


Default: content

parameters.name: X-Wait-For-Selector
parameters.description:
Specifies a CSS selector to wait for the appearance of such an element before returning.

Example: `X-Wait-For-Selector: .content-block`

parameters.name: X-Target-Selector
parameters.description:
Specifies a CSS selector for return target instead of the full html.

Implies `X-Wait-For-Selector: (same selector)`

parameters.name: X-Remove-Selector
parameters.description:
Specifies a CSS selector to remove elements from the full html.

Example `X-Remove-Selector: nav`

parameters.name: X-Keep-Img-Data-Url
parameters.description:
Keep data-url as it instead of transforming them to object-url. (Only applicable when targeting markdown format)

Example `X-Keep-Img-Data-Url: true`

parameters.name: X-Proxy-Url
parameters.description:
Specifies your custom proxy if you prefer to use one.

Supported protocols: 
- http
- https
- socks4
- socks5

For authentication, https://user:pass@host:port

parameters.name: X-Proxy-Resources
parameters.description: Whether to load resources like image/style/scripts via the proxy server.

parameters.name: X-Proxy
parameters.description:
Use a proxy server provided by us.

Optionally specify two-letter country code.

parameters.name: X-Robots-Txt
parameters.description:
Load and conform to the respective robot.txt on the target origin.

Optionally specify a bot UA to check against.

parameters.name: DNT
parameters.description: When set to 1, prevent the result of this request to be cached in the system.

parameters.name: X-Set-Cookie
parameters.description:
Sets cookie(s) to the headless browser for your request. 

Syntax is the same with standard Set-Cookie

parameters.name: X-Export-Storage-State
parameters.description:
Export the browser storage state (cookies and per-origin localStorage) accumulated during the crawl.

When enabled, the JSON response includes a `storageState` field whose shape mirrors the `storageState` request option, so it can be fed back into a subsequent request.

Requires the browser engine and disables caching.

parameters.name: X-With-Generated-Alt
parameters.description:
Enable automatic alt-text generating for images without an meaningful alt-text.

Note: Does not work when `X-Respond-With` is specified

parameters.name: X-With-Images-Summary
parameters.description: Enable dedicated summary section for images on the page.

parameters.name: X-With-links-Summary
parameters.description: Enable dedicated summary section for hyper links on the page.

parameters.name: X-Retain-Links
parameters.description:
Link retention modes.

Supported modes: 
- all: all links
- none: no links
- text: only link text
- gpt-oss: gpt-oss link citation format `【{id}†.*】`

parameters.name: X-Retain-Images
parameters.description:
Image retention modes.

Supported modes: 
- all: all images
- none: no images
- alt: only alt text
- all_p: all images and with generated alt text
- alt_p: only alt text and with generated alt

parameters.name: X-Retain-Media
parameters.description:
Media retention modes for video, audio, and embedded video iframes.

Supported modes: 
- none: no media
- text: plain label, e.g. `Video 1`
- link: markdown link, e.g. `[Video 1](url)` (default)
- image: markdown image syntax, e.g. `![Video 1](url)`
- html: original HTML with irrelevant attributes (class, id, style, data-*, aria-*) stripped

parameters.name: X-Preset
parameters.description:
Apply a preset configuration for common scenarios.

Supported presets:
- reader: optimized for display to human users
- index: optimized for semantic indexing
- research: optimized for academic/research AI agents
- agent: optimized for day-to-day AI agents
- spider: optimized for recursive site crawling

Preset values are applied only to options not explicitly set by the caller.

parameters.name: X-With-Iframe
parameters.description: Enable filling iframe contents into main. (violates standards)

parameters.name: X-With-Shadow-Dom
parameters.description: Enable filling shadow dom contents into main. (violates standards)

parameters.name: X-Skip-Cert-Verification
parameters.description: Enable skipping SSL certificate verification. (violates security best practices)

parameters.name: X-User-Agent
parameters.description:
Override User-Agent.

Several special values: 
- browser: use the internal browser UA
- auto: pass-through your UA if it starts with `Mozilla/5.0`, otherwise use the internal browser UA
- inherit / pass-through: use the User-Agent from the request context if applicable
- bot: Use a pre-defined bot User-Agent from this service
- diversify: Use a diversified browser User-Agent

Or specify your own user agent string.

Note: anonymous users specifying a browser UA will have no effect and will fall back to the internal browser UA.

Default: browser

parameters.name: X-Timeout
parameters.description: Specify timeout in seconds. Max 180.

parameters.name: X-Locale
parameters.description: Specify browser locale for the page.

parameters.name: X-Referer
parameters.description: Specify referer for the page.

parameters.name: X-Token-Budget
parameters.description:
Specify a budget in tokens.

If the resulting token cost exceeds the budget, the request is rejected.

Note this parameter is ignored for the search endpoint.

parameters.name: X-Max-Tokens
parameters.description: Trim the response content at a maximum number of tokens.

parameters.name: X-Assert-Status-Code
parameters.description: Assert the HTTP status code of the crawled page. If the actual status code does not match the asserted one, the request is rejected with 422 Unprocessable Entity.

parameters.name: X-Respond-Timing
parameters.description:
Explicitly specify the respond timing. One of the following:

- html: directly return unrendered HTML
- visible-content: return immediately when any content becomes available
- mutation-idle: wait for DOM mutations to settle and remain unchanged for at least 0.2s
- resource-idle: wait for no additional resources that would affect page logic and content has SUCCEEDED loading in 0.5s
- media-idle: wait for no additional resources, including media resources, has SUCCEEDED loading in 0.5s
- network-idle: wait for full load of webpage, also known as networkidle0.

parameters.name: X-Engine
parameters.description:
Specify the engine to use for crawling.

Supported: browser, direct, cf-browser-rendering

parameters.name: X-Base
parameters.description:
Select base modes of relative URLs.

Supported: initial, final

parameters.name: X-Remove-Overlay
parameters.description: Specify whether to remove overlay elements from the page.

parameters.name: X-Detach-Invisibles
parameters.description:
Temporarily detach elements with computed `display:none` before snapshotting, then restore them.

Requires the browser engine and disables caching.

parameters.name: X-Markdown-Chunking
parameters.description:
Opt-in markdown chunking.

Supported values: 
- true
- h1
- h2
- h3
- h4
- h5
- structured
- s1
- s2
- s3
- s4
- s5

Note if you are expecting text return, the chunking is done by injecting character \u001D

Supported: _, *

Supported: **, __

parameters.description:
Link style of the generated markdown.

This is an option passed through to [Turndown](https://github.com/mixmark-io/turndown?tab=readme-ov-file#options).

Supported: inlined, referenced, discarded

parameters.name: X-Md-Link-Reference-Style
parameters.description:
Link reference style of the generated markdown.

This is an option passed through to [Turndown](https://github.com/mixmark-io/turndown?tab=readme-ov-file#options).

Supported: full, collapsed, shortcut, discarded

parameters.name: X-Page
parameters.description:
Steer which page to return for uploaded files (PDF, DOC, XLS, PPT, etc.).

1-indexed; ignored when no file/PDF is uploaded.

parameters.name: X-Preload-Url
parameters.description:
URL to preload before scraping.

Ignored when no URL is provided.

parameters.name: X-No-Service-Worker
parameters.description:
Disable service workers when running the browser.

Useful for bypassing service-worker-based caching or interception.

EmbeddingUsage.title: EmbeddingUsage
EmbeddingUsage.description:
Token usage statistics for embedding requests.

`prompt_tokens` counts text input tokens (including the task prefix and
any structural/special framing). For text-only models — and any response
that doesn't populate a per-modality breakdown — it equals `total_tokens`.
For multimodal v5-omni responses, `total_tokens` is the aggregate across
all modalities and the per-modality fields (`image_tokens` /
`audio_tokens` / `video_tokens`) are sub-counts, so the invariant holds
exactly (absent per-modality fields count as 0):

    total_tokens == prompt_tokens + image_tokens + audio_tokens + video_tokens

PDF pages are rendered to images and counted in `image_tokens`.

All MM fields are Optional so text-only responses don't have to populate
them, and serializers should drop unset fields (`exclude_none=True`).

tags.name: Model List
tags.description: Every model this API serves, in OpenRouter-compatible form: identifiers, input and output modalities, context lengths and prices. Read it before hardcoding a model name — the catalogue moves.

tags.name: Search Foundation Models
tags.description:
**Embeddings** turn text, images, audio, video and PDFs into dense vectors for semantic search, RAG, clustering and classification. Task-specific variants (`retrieval.query`, `retrieval.passage`, `text-matching`, `clustering`, `classification`) are selected per request rather than per model, and `dimensions` truncates the output where a model supports it.

**Reranking** scores a query against a candidate set and returns it reordered, which is more accurate than embedding similarity and slower — the usual shape is embeddings to retrieve, reranking to refine.

Each endpoint's `model` field lists the models it accepts.

tags.name: Generative Models
tags.description:
Document transcription over the OpenAI chat completions schema. Point any OpenAI-compatible client at the server URL above with `/v1` appended, set `model`, and send a page image; the response is the page as text or markdown, tables and layout preserved.

`stream: true` returns server-sent events. `response_format` with a `json_schema` constrains the output to that schema instead of prose. Parameters outside the supported set are accepted and ignored rather than rejected, so an SDK-generated payload always works.

tags.name: Batch Embeddings
tags.description:
Asynchronous embedding for large workloads: up to 50,000 inputs from a GCS file URL, or 10,000 inline.

Submit with `POST /v1/batch/embeddings`, poll `GET /v1/batch/{batch_id}` until the status is `completed`, then fetch `GET /v1/batch/{batch_id}/output`. Input is OpenAI-compatible JSONL with `custom_id` and `body.input`. Output files expire after 24 hours, and a webhook can be called on completion.

tags.name: Reader
tags.description: Read a URL and get its content back in an LLM-friendly format. Put the target URL after `https://r.jina.ai/`, or pass it as `url`. Most options are `X-*` request headers.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Search the web and get the results back in an LLM-friendly format. Put the query after `https://s.jina.ai/`, or pass it as `q`. Most options are `X-*` request headers.
